strategyPosture: Hold the current posture and let the dislocation screen do the work: the index is calm but narrow (SPY -0.5% from high, IWM -5.86% over 3m), credit is loose (SLOOS 0, HY OAS 3.15%), and the actionable edge is in verified revenue-recovery names trading 28–70% below their highs — not in chasing the nuclear unwind. No new risk ahead of tomorrow's CPI with the 10-year already at 5.22%.

themes.counterRead: Equities are priced for the benign branch of tomorrow's CPI while the long end is priced for the hot branch; both cannot be right. A hot print into a 5.22% 10-year leaves equities carrying the adjustment, because HY OAS at 3.15% gives no credit-stress cushion signal either way. A soft print would instead make the 5.56% 30-year the anomaly.
themes.dataAnchor: The bond market disagrees: DGS10 is 5.22%, DGS30 is 5.56%, DGS2 is 4.75%, the 2s10s curve is +0.47, and the real 10-year is 2.89% with breakevens (T10YIE) at 2.33% — term-premium and real-rate pressure, not an inflation-expectations spiral. VIX rose +4.18% today even as SPY barely moved, and the CPI event (Oct 14) carries HIGH signal strength with hot-inflation-expectation headlines already matched.
themes.label: Long-end yields still at cycle highs into tomorrow's CPI
themes.narrative: With SPY at 776.87, down only -0.16% today, and VIX at 15.46, the equity market believes the rates story is settled and tomorrow's CPI Sep 2026 print is a formality.
themes.watchFor: Tomorrow's CPI print versus the hot-expectation headlines, and whether DGS10 holds above 5.2% or pushes toward 5.5% on the release.

themes.counterRead: Price and fundamentals are moving in opposite directions in exactly the names with confirmed revenue recovery — that is the opportunity setup, not a value-trap signal. The discipline is the screen's own caveat: the pullback posture is RESEARCH_SCREENED, meaning every candidate passed the 5-gate screen but the thesis still has to be verified name-by-name before sizing; a sentiment label is not itself evidence.
themes.dataAnchor: The fundamentals say otherwise for the screen leaders. AVGO (a holding) sits -28% from its 52-week high with revenue growing +55% YoY, 67.8% gross margin, $26,914M FCF at a 42.1% margin, and a conviction score of 81 (Tier A) — the top-ranked name. APP is -63.2% from its high with revenue +55.8% YoY on the watchlist screen (RSI 33.6), NOW is -27.5% with revenue +23.1% YoY, NXT is -46.4% with revenue +31.6% YoY, and KTOS is -69.7% with revenue +26.9% YoY. All five carry RECOVERY revenue inflections and were promoted on the watchlist this run.
themes.label: AI-infrastructure and software dislocations: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The tape treats the AI-infrastructure and enterprise-software complex as broken momentum: 24 tracked dislocations are flagged, most labeled SENTIMENT_DRIVEN, implying the drawdowns are information.
themes.watchFor: Any of AVGO, APP, NOW, NXT, or KTOS losing its RECOVERY revenue inflection on the next earnings print, or price basing with RSI holding above its drawdown low.

themes.counterRead: The calm is narrow, not broad: large-cap price is ahead of the breadth data, but loose credit (SLOOS 0, HY OAS 3.15%) says this is divergence, not yet a rollover. If lending standards tighten off 0 or HY OAS widens materially from 3.15% while IWM stays negative, the same narrowness becomes the leading edge of a rollover instead of rotation.
themes.dataAnchor: Breadth underneath is weak: IWM is -4.04% over 1 month and -5.86% over 3 months while SPY is +3.7% over 3 months and QQQ is +4.19% over 3 months. The Mag7 average still sits -8.43% from its 52-week high versus SPY at -0.5% (a -7.93-point gap), with TSLA weakest at -24.8% and MSFT strongest at -1.3%. Credit does not confirm stress — SLOOS lending standards are LOOSE at 0 and HY OAS is tight at 3.15%.
themes.label: Index calm is narrow: small caps keep falling behind
themes.narrative: SPY at 776.87, just -0.5% from its 52-week high and +2.1% over the past month, reads as broad market health, and the concentration state has eased to NO_SIGNIFICANT_DIVERGENCE.
themes.watchFor: IWM 1-month performance turning positive from -4.04%, or HY OAS widening above 4% while the Mag7-to-SPY gap stays beyond -7 points.

themes.counterRead: The unwind is concentrated in the narrative-heavy, pre-profit names (SMR, OKLO, ASTS) while the cash-generating incumbent VST holds a strongly positive 1-month trend — the market is repricing story duration, not abandoning the power theme. Chasing the falling names is catching the side where narrative was furthest ahead of data; the theme only becomes interesting again when the laggards stop making new 1-month lows.
themes.dataAnchor: The 1-month laggard list is dominated by the complex: SMR -23.56%, ASTS -21.38% (and -8.34% today alone), OKLO -12.34%, and URA -11.61%. Holding VST diverges sharply the other way — a 1-month leader at +14.66%, +2.04% today, with a +15.3% dislocation trend and RSI 63.4 — and PLTR (+20.17% 1m), META (+14.59%), and GEV (+13.5%) lead the tape instead.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI-power momentum unwind, incumbent diverging
themes.narrative: The nuclear and AI-power complex was priced as the purest AI-electricity trade; the market believed the story had years of runway without interruption.
themes.watchFor: SMR and OKLO posting a flat-to-positive day on a down tape, or VST losing its +14.66% 1-month trend and joining the laggards — the first signals stabilization, the second that the unwind is spreading to quality.

themes.counterRead: This is the control case for the whole dislocation screen: where the decline has a confirmed fundamental cause, price and data agree and there is no gap to harvest. Treating TMDX as interchangeable with the sentiment-driven names would import exactly the error the screen exists to avoid — verify the decline reason before treating any single dislocation as opportunity.
themes.dataAnchor: The one high-materiality news item in the entire input contradicts the label: TMDX dipped after posting a Q1 earnings and revenue miss with falling margins (materiality score 8, the only high-materiality item). Unlike AVGO or APP, TMDX does not appear in top conviction or the watchlist promotions, so there is no offsetting revenue-recovery figure in the conviction data.
themes.label: TMDX: the dislocation screen's exception — this decline is fundamental
themes.narrative: TMDX screens like the rest of the dislocation list — -48.8% from its 52-week high, RSI 43.9, classified SENTIMENT_DRIVEN with a FULL_SIGNAL — implying the market has overshot on mood.
themes.watchFor: A subsequent TMDX print showing revenue growth re-accelerating and margins stabilizing, which would move it from fundamental decline to genuine dislocation.

HY OAS widening from 3.15% or SLOOS lending standards moving off 0 — either flips narrow calm into rollover risk
IWM 1-month performance recovering from -4.04% toward positive, versus the Mag7-to-SPY gap widening past -12 points
AVGO, APP, NOW, NXT, KTOS: revenue inflection staying at RECOVERY on next prints, and price basing rather than extending drawdowns
SMR/OKLO stabilization (a non-negative day on a down tape) versus VST losing its +14.66% 1-month trend
whereWaveBuilds: The next move most likely materializes around tomorrow's CPI print colliding with a 5.22% 10-year and 5.56% 30-year: a hot print forces equities to do the adjusting the bond market has already done, while a soft print releases the most pressure exactly where dislocations are deepest (AVGO, APP, NOW). The FOMC decision on Oct 27–28 is the second trigger on the calendar.
